reason: E3 directly supports the link between lattice strain and unusual dislocation behaviors for strength-ductility synergy. E2 supports nano-twinning as a deformation mode that helps maintain toughness at high strength. However, no cited evidence demonstrates the combined interaction of lattice strain, dislocations, and nano-twinning governing toughness, nor that controlled strain introduction optimizes this interaction. E1 is about plastic deformation in ceramics and is misrepresented as evidence for the alloy hypothesis.
premises: Heterogeneous lattice strain causes unusual dislocation behaviors (multiple kinks/jogs, bidirectional cross slips) leading to strength-ductility synergy
Nano-twinning contributes an additional deformation mode that alleviates the deleterious effects of high strength on toughness
The interaction between lattice strain, dislocation behavior, and nano-twinning governs toughness retention or loss
Controlled introduction of lattice strain via composition engineering or deformation can optimize this interaction
